schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A1 INT, A2 INT);
q1: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.A1 AND X.A2 = Y.A2
q2: SELECT DISTINCT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X, R AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.A1 AND X.A2 = Y.A2
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2 FROM R AS X
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects distinct pairs (A1, A2) from table R where there are at least two rows with the same A1 and A2 values. Q2 simply selects all distinct pairs (A1, A2) from table R without any conditions.
counterexample_dsp: A counterexample can be created by inserting at least two rows with the same A1 and A2 values into table R.
